questions.question: 1. What key factor determines the minimum separation distance required between co-channel cells?

answers.a: The physical size of the cell tower
answers.c: The number of users in the cell
answers.d: The type of mobile phone being used

questions.question: 2. A small cluster size implies what about the number of cells within that cluster?

answers.c: The number of cells is variable and unrelated

questions.question: 3. What technique involves subdividing a congested cell into smaller cells to increase capacity?
4. What is the primary purpose of implementing 'cell sectoring' at a base station?

answers.a: To increase the geographic size of a single cell
answers.c: To allow all cells to use the same frequency
answers.d: To decrease the number of cell towers

questions.question: 5. How does cell sectoring primarily achieve its goal of reducing interference?

answers.a: By increasing the power of the transmitted signal
answers.c: By making the cells physically smaller
answers.d: By assigning different frequencies to each sector

questions.question: 6. What is a common trade-off or disadvantage of implementing cell sectoring?

answers.a: It reduces the total capacity of the cell
answers.b: It increases the number of handoffs for moving users
answers.c: It requires all users to have special phones
answers.d: It completely eliminates the need for co-channel cells

questions.question: 7. How might a large natural obstruction, like a mountain, affect co-channel interference?

answers.a: It would significantly increase the interference
answers.b: It would have no effect on interference
answers.c: It could decrease the interference by blocking the signal path
answers.d: It would change the frequencies used by the cells

questions.question: 8. Why is a cluster size of one, where every cell uses all available frequencies, generally avoided?

answers.a: It would cause unmanageably high co-channel interference
answers.b: It is too complex to build the base stations
answers.c: It would provide very low system capacity
answers.d: It would require very large, tall cell towers

questions.question: 9. In a cellular system using frequency reuse, the signal-to-interference ratio can be best improved by...

answers.a: decreasing the power of all base stations.
answers.b: increasing the distance between co-channel cells.
answers.c: decreasing the distance between co-channel cells.

questions.question: 10. When 'cell splitting' is performed, what typically happens to the original cluster size?

answers.a: The cluster size must be increased
answers.b: The cluster size must be decreased
answers.c: The cluster size can remain the same
answers.d: The concept of a cluster is eliminated
